title: Key synchronization drift caused missing audit entries during SSO cert refresh
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the SSO certificate refresh window on 2026-02-28 02:10–05:30 UTC a subset of audit events generated by auth-proxy and the sign-in service were not persisted to the primary audit index for ~3 hours. The problem was detected by the security monitoring alert (alert: audit-write-drop-rate) and by customers reporting missing access events in compliance exports.

Impact:
- Missing audit entries for ~3.1k authentication-related events across 2026-02-28 02:12–05:08 UTC.
- Exports to customer compliance buckets for two enterprise customers were incomplete (affected exports have been re-run).
- No evidence of tampering; no keys were leaked. This is a availability/completeness incident for audit records (regulatory risk).

Detection & timeline (high level):
- 02:10 UTC: Automated SSO cert rotation initiated (staggered across regions).
- 02:11–02:15 UTC: Key sync controller began applying new cert metadata across services.
- 02:20 UTC: First signs of elevated audit write error rates from auth-proxy; noisy logs indicated producer rejections.
- 02:45 UTC: On-call escalated to security-ops after alert; initial mitigation: pause next rotation wave and re-enable previous certs for affected region.
- 03:30 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis identified (see below).
- 04:00 UTC: Backfill job started to reingest buffered events; write-through to index resumed by 05:30 UTC after confirmation of successful reingestion and validation.

Root cause (investigation summary):
Primary cause is a key synchronization drift combined with a producer TTL mismatch: the key-sync controller uses a revision token for ordering updates. A subtle bug in the controller meant that under heavy rotation concurrency the controller could re-apply an older revision after a delayed reconciliation, causing the local audit producer to see a transient mismatch between its active signing key and the key metadata served by the KMS proxy. When producers detected the mismatch they temporarily stamped events with a fallback unsigned marker and forwarded them to the buffering tier. The buffering tier had a short retention (30 minutes) and an internal compaction ran during the incident window which discarded some of the fallback-marked frames because they appeared to be duplicate tombstones. Two factors combined to cause final persistence loss: (1) out-of-order key application (drift) and (2) insufficient buffer retention and compaction rules for fallback-marked events.

Mitigations performed during incident:
- Rotation waves paused and a targeted rollback of the key-sync controller to the pre-rotation revision.
- Immediately increased buffer retention from 30m to 6h and disabled compaction for legacy fallback markers.
- Triggered reingest/backfill job that consumed retained events and republished to the audit index.
- Notified affected customers and re-ran compliance exports for impacted windows.

Longer-term action items (this ticket):
1) Fix key-sync controller ordering logic: enforce monotonic revision apply and add idempotent apply guards (ENG-77322).
2) Harden producer behavior: producers should avoid emitting fallback-unmarked frames; add backpressure/queue metrics and fail-open only after documented retries (ENG-77323).
3) Increase audit buffer retention to 24h for regions participating in rotation, and revise compaction rules to never drop fallback-marked frames until reingest confirmation is persisted (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/KeySync+Audit+Buffer+Design).
4) Add a canary gating step to the cert rotation runbook: run a write-read loop verification in a canary subset of auth-proxy instances before advancing waves (playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Rotation+Canary+Playbook).
5) Create an end-to-end integration test that simulates rotation + buffer compaction and asserts no loss (CI job: ci/security/audit-rotation-regen).
6) Add metric and alert: "audit-ingest-lag" with SLO threshold and an automated pager escalation if unacked buffer backlog exceeds 15 minutes.
7) Post-release audit: run a one-week verification job to reconcile expected vs persisted audit counts by service (dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/SEC/audit-integrity).
8) Security review of rotation automation and RBAC for KMS proxy (blocked until review complete).

Acceptance criteria for close:
- Patch merged and deployed for key-sync controller with monotonic ordering and idempotency checks.
- Producer changes merged and rolled to 50% canary, no regressions observed after 72h.
- Buffer retention and compaction changes live in prod and verified by the parity job.
- Playbook updated and security review completed.
- Postmortem page published with customer notifications and export proofs.

Artifacts and links:
- Incident timeline & postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/2026-02-28+SSO+Rotation+Audit+Gap
- Backfill job PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-backfill/pull/142
- Key-sync controller fix PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/key-sync/pull/88
- Canary playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Rotation+Canary+Playbook
- Integrity dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/SEC/audit-integrity

Notes / trade-offs considered:
- We initially considered turning off compaction globally — rejected due to long-term storage cost; instead we limit compaction exceptions to fallback-marked events.
- Extending retention to 24h increases ephemeral storage cost but reduces regulatory risk significantly; recommended as default for rotation waves only.
- We debated immediate forced reingest for all regions vs targeted reingest; chose targeted due to risk of duplicate writes and downstream indexing load.
